name: Small decision bodies: closed-electorate selection, coalition bargaining and committee-vote simulators
one_line: Structure-first models of small electorates (Nobel committee, conclave, UNSC, party caucus, coalition partners, FOMC voters, pivotal senators), with LLMs only filling actor tables or playing electors, to sell structurally dead longshots, price coalition ladders through their exact rule and price dissent / vote-count brackets; unproven, and on 20 resolved events the market's sub-10c names were already calibrated.
maturity: Experimental; one published structural ranking (Soda et al.) had the conclave winner among its top three at 1.15% while its other two top names lost; a rival structural model picked Parolin because its candidate list omitted Prevost; committee twins never compared with a market; nobody trades it
requires_ai: optional; LLMs fill actor tables and play electors; structure, solver, rule mapping deterministic
edge: Hypothetical: selecting which sub-10c names are structurally dead; rule-aware coalition mapping
capital: <$1k to test, $2-10k to trade; capacity-bound (~$150 median within 5c per name), months of lock-up
build_time: 1-2 weeks per body (structure layer); 4-8 weeks solo for selection, coalition and committee families
opportunity_size: Nobel Peace 2026 $25.1M (30 sub-10c names); FOMC dissents $61-82k/meeting vs $144-284M decisions; ~8 events/year
expected_results: no public data, theoretical only; unselected sub-10c short basket +0.1%/contract at 7 days at the mid, ~-0.1% after a 0.2c half-spread; guess -$50 to +$30/month
competition: no simulator trader found; name-recognition retail, bookmakers, late leakers set prices
flag: grey; leaks / MNPI dominate n=1 events; election-contract restrictions; tail risk
validate: Masked retro-test plus forward paper basket; kill if structure-flagged basket = unselected FLB basket (~230 flagged names needed)
top_risk: Leak-driven hits on sub-1c names; no aggregate longshot bias to select
solo_fit_reason: The structure-only arm is cheap and leak-proof to retro-test, but the family resolves ~8 events a year on Polymarket, its sub-10c names are already calibrated in aggregate (2 hits vs 2.1-3.0 implied per horizon), the two big surprises were priced below 1c and one was a leak (Machado 2c to 73c nine hours early), and the public-vote side has $0 within 5c on the middle dissent brackets; power needs years of flow.
speed_class: speed-insensitive: slow structure; resting book execution-sensitive in last 24 h (leaks)
results_5k: marginal; -$200 to +$45/month, depth and leaks bind (guess)
min_capital: $0 until the retro-test passes; ~$2-3k after, for per-event caps
capacity_ceiling: ~$5-10k: ~30 sub-10c Nobel names x $150-300 within 5c plus small books
services: Data API v2 resolutions + Gamma umaResolutionStatuses
public rosters and records (Vatican, Fed, Senate, manifestos)
changes_made: Written 2026-09-29 with live checks: Gamma public-search for live selection, coalition, Fed dissent, SCOTUS, shutdown, deal and ceasefire markets (Nobel Peace 2026 $25.1M / 71 names, UNSG $206k, TIME 2026 $89k, Swedish coalition and party ladders, Fed October dissent $7.7k vs decision $16.05M); CLOB books on 54 live markets (sub-10c names median ~$150 within 5c; dissent brackets 1 and 2 $0 within 5c).

Own baseline: 20 resolved selection / party-leader / coalition events (Nov 2023 - May 2026, $457M, 517 markets incl. 10 FOMC dissent events and one confirmation vote count), CLOB prices-history at T-30/7/1 days conditioned on the market existing at t; market Brier 0.044 / 0.028 / 0.032; sub-10c names 2 hits vs 2.14 implied at 7 days, unselected short basket +0.13% per contract [-1.21, +1.55], +1.03% per event [-0.21, +2.22]; both hits (Machado, Prevost) priced below 1c; the paper's per-event sign flip cannot be tested with two hits.

Leak paths measured: Machado 2.1c at 21:00 UTC to 73c at 00:00 UTC, nine hours before the 2025 announcement (CoinDesk: Nobel Institute 'prey to a criminal actor'); TIME 2024 and 2025 winners 98-99c the evening before the reveal day; the $1.86M 'Will Time 2025 POY be leaked?' market resolved Yes after two disputes.

FOMC dissents: market five-bracket Brier 0.676 / 0.602 at T-7 / T-1 days vs a leave-future-out base rate 0.874 over 8 meetings; volume $2.6M over 10 meetings vs $144-284M per decision market; Kalshi dissent counts 281k-487k contracts per event.

Adjacent field fetched: Soda et al. (Prevost 1st status, 2nd mediation, 8th coalition; Polymarket 1.15%; published 7 May 2025), Antonioni et al. (picked Parolin), Crokidakis, Digital Pantheon, Kulkarni, FedSight, Takano, Collodel, Kreutner, Helm, Katz (PLOS ONE), Foresight Arena; BDM 90% CIA figure traced to his own Foreign Policy article via Wikipedia; GitHub searches found no simulator connected to Polymarket or Kalshi.

Critic notes addressed: merged decision-body member twins as the public-vote section with capacity stated; added bilateral deadline bargaining with the hazard part routed to file 70; stated that this is an institutional twin, not polling; Gamma searches (active and closed) found no SEC / FCC / FTC commission-vote or FDA advisory-panel vote markets, only approval outcomes; named-senator ladders exist (Clarity Act $210k) and Kalshi lists confirmation vote counts.

Cite-check + skeptic pass 2026-09-29 (25 of 25 numbered sources re-fetched or re-queried: 13 arXiv abstracts via the export API, Soda v2 and Antonioni v2 and Digital Pantheon v2 and Foresight Arena v2 full text, PLOS ONE, Wikipedia, CoinDesk, Polymarket fee docs, GitHub API, Gamma events / public-search, Kalshi API; 0 removed, 0 unreachable): Digital Pantheon corrected (partners fixed; it simulates influence over the agreement text, never which coalition forms); SCOTUS model is +2.7 points over the 67.5% memory null, not ~5; Antonioni et al.'s candidate list omitted Prevost (added as a structural-model failure mode alongside the 2024 Literature 'Other' winner); Swedish MP gap shown to close at executable prices (MP options 52.5c bid / 63.2c ask vs party market 63/64c); UNSG and Swedish coalition liquidity corrected ($11k and $27k, not $106k and $276k); Machado path 49-71c (not 66-71c) before the announcement; TIME 2024/2025 moves no longer called leaks without checking for a press report; conclave straw-poll cost $8-80 (was $5-60); Lamparth marked pre-2025. Baseline re-run: all headline numbers reproduce (analyse.py, analyse_bands.py, analyse_fed_leak.py); adding the excluded $40.9M 'Next Chancellor of Germany' event moves the short-basket figures by <= 0.07 points; no multi-name 2024 Nobel Peace market exists on Polymarket (only a UNRWA yes/no); basket returns flagged as mid-price (a 0.2c half-spread turns +0.13% into about -0.1% per contract); outcome-defined T clock flagged and Phase 1 re-anchored on scheduled announcements; leak rule: the >= 3c/hour trigger would fire only after 2-4c asks were lifted on the Machado path, the 24-hour pre-announcement cancel is the rule that works. Power figures re-derived (230 names / ~40 events; 45-80 events from SD 2.4-9.6; ~200 FOMC meetings from SD ~0.5). 15-field part 2,722 -> 2,604 words.
open_doubts: Horizons in the baseline are anchored on the first hour the winner held >= 0.90 (an outcome-defined clock); for staged coalition outcomes this moves horizons weeks before the formal decision.

Only 20 resolved events with 2 longshot hits: basket returns and per-event SDs are understated and the per-event FLB sign flip cannot be tested; Kalshi's Nobel / TIME / coalition archives were not replayed.

Returns use hourly prices-history mids, not executable quotes; at a 0.2c half-spread the unselected short basket is slightly negative, and maker fills on sub-10c names are adversely selected by leakers.
Whether TIME 2024 / 2025 late moves followed public press reports or private information was not checked; official reveal times were not fetched.
The Swedish MP gap is a mid-price discrepancy inside the ladder spreads; its persistence after the formal deadline difference is unexplained.
Straw-poll and elicitation costs are estimates from file 21's list prices, not measured runs.
